subject: computer-science
title: Normalisation: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF
welcome_lead: Cut redundancy and prevent anomalies, one form at a time.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: first, second and third normal forms.
final_note: Normalised data updates cleanly and stays consistent.

concepts.def: Atomic values only — no repeating groups or lists in a cell.
1NF plus no partial dependencies on a composite key.
2NF plus no transitive dependencies — non-key attributes depend only on the key.
A non-key attribute depending on another non-key attribute.
An update, insert or delete problem caused by redundant data.

walkthroughs.body_html: 1NF requires atomic values. Replace a 'phones' column containing '01234, 05678' with separate rows or a related phones table.
2NF (when there is a composite key) requires every non-key attribute to depend on the whole key, not part of it. Otherwise split the partial dependency into its own table.
3NF removes transitive dependencies. If StudentID -> CourseID -> Tutor, store the Tutor with the Course, not the Student.
